candidates.detail: The current authored item catalog has a malformed escaped display_name for lubeck_mark. Parsing its JSON-compatible text yields a multi-character mojibake sequence in place of ü, whereas the nearby current inventory source assertion labels this authored currency as Lübeck mark. The item compiler reads YAML-named files as strict JSON values, validates and serializes the documents; ItemDefinition retains display_name as String. At runtime the catalog definition lookup supplies that field to currency_name and item_display_name. This is source and evidence-byte analysis; no build, parser under product execution, browser or UI was run.
candidates.ui_path: For an existing lubeck_mark currency row, item_name_with_quality renders a generic Coin label plus a data-currency-name attribute from currency_name. The inventory browser groups currency rows and copies that attribute to the denomination row when expanded. A target control and quest transfer labels also use item_display_name. Thus the traced source predicts malformed denomination/accessible text when those conditions and successful catalog compilation are met; no particular stock, inventory state, live interaction or rendered output was observed.
candidates.bounded_scan: A mechanical search for the characters U+00C3, U+00C2 or U+FFFD in display_name fields of this one current catalog found nine IDs: lubeck_mark, primer_german_latin, primer_latin_german, primer_low_german, primer_german_low, german_herbal, kitchen_book, tailors_pattern_book and smiths_handbook. This is a marker-based inventory, not a complete encoding audit or proof of every intended spelling. Current and frozen pr-working catalogs have the same nine marker IDs but different decoded values; each version is preserved separately.
candidates.safeguards: The inventory initially groups denomination labels as Coin, and currency IDs remain stable; the traced concern is presentation text, not currency value or identity. The source assertion checks that the row contains whatever catalog currency_name returns; its descriptive expect message does not independently compare the name to the intended Unicode string. The validator checks required nonempty names and a maximum byte length, not editorial correctness. Other displays, catalog documents and plausible non-Latin text remain unassessed.
candidates.connected_scope: Authored UTF-8/JSON-compatible item catalog and content-generation provenance; build-time strict parse/validation and embedded serialization; ItemDefinition lookup; currency grouping, item labels, accessibility labels and any other catalog presentation consumers.
candidates.proposed_repair: After audit completion and implementation authorization, establish the intended names from authoritative item content and repair the affected authored text and any content-generation step that introduced re-encoding. Preserve valid international characters and stable IDs; do not normalize every non-ASCII name or add a blind compatibility decoder.
